From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit & evals — Redwood benchmark links

Hi Olivia — great to meet you on the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: low-latency conversational summarization for customer support transcripts (avg input length ~1,200 tokens, generation target ~150 tokens).
- Qs: strict PII handling, SLA targets (p50 < 200ms for typical requests), and a concern about quality regressions when switching quantized model variants.

Recommended starting point (model + config)
- redwood-13b-v2 (q4f16) — best balance of quality and cost for your prompt set.
- redwood-7b-chat (q4_kv) — lower latency option for lower-cost lanes; good for higher throughput non-critical paths.

Redwood-verified performance (baseline, per-GPU steady-state for 256-token generations):
- redwood-13b-v2 (q4f16): TPS ~750 tokens/sec, p50=85ms, p90=180ms, p99=420ms
- redwood-7b-chat (q4_kv): TPS ~1,300 tokens/sec, p50=55ms, p90=120ms, p99=310ms

Attachments & links
- Attached: redwood_benchmark_report_v1.pdf (end-to-end benchmark on representative prompts)
- Prompt sets & eval harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cPromptSets
- Benchmark dashboard (Redwood Console): https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/FB-2026-1134

Concerns & mitigations
- Quality regressions with quantization: we recommend a two-stage approach — run your prompt set against both fp16 and q4f16 variants, compare automated metrics (ROUGE/ROUGE-L, embedding similarity) + spot-checks. We can run these evals for you as a scoped SE engagement.
- PII & security: Redwood Private can be provisioned for FinBank if you need customer-managed networking and KMS; we also provide per-token auditing.

Proposed next steps
1) Marissa to run a focused benchmark on the prompt set you shared (same corpus as today) and return a short findings doc (expected 3 business days).
2) Schedule a 30-min follow-up demo with small-scale live inference to validate latency at 95th percentile.
3) If results look good, we’ll scope a pilot with dedicated capacity (estimated 2-4 weeks).

Would you be available next Tuesday (7/7) 10–10:30am PT for the demo?

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia — thanks for the questions, quick answers below and links to the artifacts we referenced.

1) Prompt sets: uploaded to the Drive folder ("finbank_prompt_set_v1.json") — link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cPromptSets. I’ve attached a copy (prompt_sets_v1.json) for quick reference.

2) Latency baseline: the numbers I quoted are from our hosted Dedicated A100 profiles (256-token gen). H100s will likely improve p50/p90 by ~10–30% depending on kernel stack. We’ll validate on your hardware as part of the pilot.

3) Quality/regression checklist (short):
- Run automated metrics on your eval set: ROUGE-L, BLEURT/embedding cosine vs. current baseline
- Sample-based blind evals (randomly sample 50 outputs, have SMEs rate for correctness and hallucination)
- Monitor n-gram novelty and entity hallucination counts
- Validate prompt templates + redaction pipeline end-to-end against PII test cases

Benchmarks & perf profiles (public links)
- Console dashboard (live): https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/FB-2026-1134
- Performance profile CSV (attached: redwood_perf_profiles.csv) — includes per-model TPS and latency percentiles used in the report

Proposed immediate action: Marissa, can you run the focused benchmark on the finbank_prompt_set_v1.json and include both fp16 and q4f16 model variants? Output should include: latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec), and automated quality metrics. Target turnaround: EOD Fri (7/3).

Olivia — I’ll leave scheduling for Tue 7/7 10am PT on the calendar — sending invite now.

Thanks — Alex
